questions.solution:
To solve the inequality |x - 3| < 4, consider two cases: when (x - 3) is positive and when it's negative.

Case 1: x - 3 ≥ 0
(x - 3) < 4
x < 7
Combine with x ≥ 3 to get [3, 7).

Case 2: x - 3 < 0
-(x - 3) < 4
-x + 3 < 4
x > -1
Combine with x < 3 to get (-∞, 3).

The solution is -1 < x < 7.
questions.explanation: Account for both cases where the absolute value expression can be positive or negative. Choice B assumes OR (incorrect), C only considers equality, and D misses the solution.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Not considering both cases in absolute value inequality.

questions.solution:
Consider two cases: when (2x + 5) is positive and when it's negative.

Case 1: 2x + 5 ≥ 0
2x + 5 ≤ 10
2x ≤ 5
x ≤ 2.5
Combine with x ≥ -2.5 to get [-2.5, 2.5].

Case 2: 2x + 5 < 0
-(2x + 5) ≤ 10
-2x - 5 ≤ 10
-2x ≤ 15
x ≥ -7.5
Combine with x < -2.5 to get [-7.5, ∞).

The solution is -7.5 ≤ x ≤ 2.5.
questions.explanation: Account for both cases and find the intersection of ranges. Choice B only considers equality, C misunderstands ≤, D misses solution.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Not considering both cases in absolute value inequality.

questions.solution:
For |3x - 1| > 7, only one case: 3x - 1 > 7 or 3x - 1 < -7.

3x > 8 or 3x < -6
x > 8/3 or x < -2.
Solution is x < -2 or x > 8.

questions.common_mistake_notes: Assuming two cases in absolute value inequality when only one is needed.

questions.solution:
Two cases: when (4x - 6) is positive and when it's negative.

Case 1: 4x - 6 ≥ 0
4x - 6 ≥ 10
4x ≥ 16
x ≥ 4
Combine with x ≥ 1.5 to get [4, ∞).

Case 2: 4x - 6 < 0
-(4x - 6) ≥ 10
-4x + 6 ≥ 10
-4x ≥ 4
x ≤ -1
Combine with x < 1.5 to get (-∞, -1].

Solution is x ≤ -1 or x ≥ 4.
